See Robert L. Millet,Becoming New: A Doctrinal Commentary on the Writings of Paul(2022), 97–98, 134. Some have suggested that the members of the Church in Corinth were influenced by early ideas that the “body is a tomb”(Greeksōma sēmas) and that the physical body was worthless and was not needed in the next life. These views were known in the first century, when Paul was writing to the Corinthians (see Flavius Josephus,War of the Jews, trans. William Whiston [1875], 2.8.11).
